gates.title: An equation is a constraint, not an instruction to compute

canonical_concepts.statement: An equation in one unknown is a statement that is true for some values of the unknown and false for others; solving means finding exactly those values.
The equals sign asserts that two expressions have the same value; it does not mean 'compute the left side'.

relations.expression: S = { x in Q : a*x + b = c }
relations.meaning: The solution set is the collection of admissible values making the statement true.

symbols.meaning: The unknown
The solution set
Given rational coefficients

conditions: The domain of the unknown is declared before the set is described.
A different declared domain can change the solution set.

required_labels.label: declared positive direction along the line

representations.verification_method: Substitute the marked value back into the original statement and confirm both sides agree exactly.
must_not_imply: That a solution drawn between two ticks is approximately equal to either of them.
That every equation has exactly one solution.

validity_conditions: The domain of the unknown is declared.

reasoning_sequence.action: Declare the domain the unknown ranges over.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: A solution set has no meaning until the admissible values are fixed.

reasoning_sequence.action: Substitute a candidate and check whether the statement becomes true.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Membership of the solution set is decided by substitution, which is the definition.

transformations.statement: Substituting a value turns an equation into a numerical statement that is simply true or false.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: The equals sign means 'work out the left-hand side and write the result on the right'.
misconceptions.counterexample: In 3x + 2 = 9 there is nothing to work out on the left until x is known; the statement constrains x instead.
misconceptions.repair: Read the statement aloud as 'three times the unknown, plus two, is nine' and test a value by substitution before manipulating anything.

problem_families.title: Decide whether a given value satisfies an equation
hidden_invariants: Substitution decides membership; rearrangement is not required.

difficulty.note: Conceptually foundational and frequently skipped, which is why later sign and division errors are so hard to diagnose.

falsification_cases.mutation: Remove the domain field from a relation symbol.
Cite a representation kind the Mathematics contract does not declare.

gates.title: Which operations preserve the solution set

canonical_concepts.statement: Adding the same quantity to both sides, or multiplying both sides by a non-zero quantity, leaves the solution set unchanged.
Multiplying both sides by zero destroys information: every value then satisfies the result.

relations.meaning: Subtracting b from both sides and dividing both sides by a non-zero a isolates the unknown without changing which values satisfy the statement.

symbols.meaning: Coefficient of the unknown; must not be zero
Constant added on the left
Value the left side must equal
The unknown

conditions: a is non-zero; if a = 0 the statement is either never true or always true.
Both operations are reversible, which is why the solution set is preserved.

required_labels.label: declared positive direction along the line

representations.verification_method: Substitute the isolated value into the original statement, not into an intermediate line.
must_not_imply: That every rearrangement preserves the solution set.

validity_conditions: Coefficients and the unknown share the declared rational domain.

reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Adding the same quantity to both sides is reversible, so no solution is gained or lost.

reasoning_sequence.action: Divide both sides by a, having checked a is non-zero.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Dividing by a non-zero quantity is reversible; dividing by zero is undefined.

reasoning_sequence.action: Substitute the result into the original statement.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Verification against the original catches an error made in any intermediate line.

transformations.statement: An operation preserves the solution set exactly when it can be undone on both sides.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: You may divide both sides by any expression, including one containing the unknown.
misconceptions.counterexample: From x*x = x, dividing both sides by x gives x = 1 and loses the solution x = 0.
misconceptions.repair: Before dividing, state that the divisor is non-zero; if it might be zero, treat that case separately instead of dividing.

problem_families.title: Isolate the unknown in a one-step or two-step linear equation

falsification_cases.mutation: Make the isolate step depend on the verify step.

gates.title: An exact solution and its decimal approximation are different objects

canonical_concepts.statement: A rational solution is a single exact number; writing it as a fraction is not an unfinished answer.
A decimal approximation that changes the exact rational value is a different number; an exact terminating decimal is another notation for the same rational.

relations.expression: x exact  =>  a*x + b = c holds exactly
relations.meaning: For a nonzero linear coefficient, the residual is a times the error in the candidate value. An exact terminating decimal is an exact rational too; only a changed value introduces a nonzero residual.

symbols.meaning: The exact rational solution
A decimal approximation of that solution
symbols.domain: the terminating decimals, a proper subset of Q

conditions: The linear coefficient a is non-zero and all arithmetic is exact over the rationals.
The decimal approximation differs numerically from the exact solution.
Rounding is a presentation choice made after the mathematics, never during it.

required_labels.label: declared positive direction along the line

representations.verification_method: Show the exact value strictly between two integers and confirm neither integer satisfies the equation.
must_not_imply: That a value between two ticks equals the nearer tick.
That a fraction is a less finished answer than a decimal.

validity_conditions: The declared domain is the rationals.
Exactness claims concern the value, not its written form.

reasoning_sequence.action: Record the solution as an exact fraction in lowest terms.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: The division that produced it need not terminate as a decimal.

reasoning_sequence.action: Verify by substituting the exact fraction.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Exact substitution reproduces the original statement with no residue.

reasoning_sequence.action: Compare an exact terminating decimal with a numerically changed approximation.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Notation alone changes no value; a changed value has residual a times its error.

transformations.statement: Reducing a fraction to lowest terms changes its written form, not the number it names.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: A fraction should be converted to a decimal to give the real answer.
misconceptions.counterexample: For 3x + 2 = 9 the solution is 7/3; substituting 2.333333333333 gives 8.999999999999, not 9.
misconceptions.repair: Substitute both the fraction and the truncated decimal into the original statement and compare the two results exactly.

problem_families.title: Solve a linear equation whose solution is not a terminating decimal
hidden_invariants: The exact value verifies; the truncation does not.

difficulty.note: The arithmetic is easy; distinguishing the two objects is the actual content.

falsification_cases.mutation: Reuse REL-EQ-LINEAR-SOLUTION as a relation id in this gate.
Change scope_class to PRESCRIBED with no curriculum binding.

gates.title: Declared-domain equality operations and real-plane line boundaries

canonical_concepts.statement: Reversible operations preserve the declared solution set; real-plane line equations include either single zero coefficient but exclude both zero.

relations.expression: s is a solution of L(x) = R(x)  ⇔  L(s) = R(s)
relations.meaning: A number is a solution exactly when the LHS and the RHS take the same value at it; the equation is true only for such values, and a proposed solution is confirmed by substituting it back into the original equation.

symbols.meaning: The one variable of the equation
The linear expression on the left-hand side
The linear expression on the right-hand side
The candidate value being tested

conditions: The statement is an equation: an equality sign stands between two expressions in the variable.
Both sides are linear expressions in one variable only.
The equality is not assumed to hold for every value; only an identity does that.

relations.expression: L = R has the same solution as L + c = R + c, L − c = R − c, kL = kR and L ÷ k = R ÷ k (k ≠ 0); transposing: L + t = R ⇔ L = R − t
relations.meaning: Doing the same thing to both sides keeps the balance, so the solution is unchanged; subtracting a term from both sides is the same as transposing it to the other side, and variable terms can be transposed just like numbers.

symbols.meaning: The left-hand and right-hand expressions of the equation
A number added to or subtracted from both sides
A number both sides are multiplied or divided by
A term (a number or a variable term) moved across the equality sign

conditions: The same operation is applied to the whole of both sides, never to one side only.
A number that multiplies or divides both sides is non-zero.
A transposed term changes its sign, because transposing is subtracting (or adding) it on both sides.

relations.expression: L = R  ⇔  m·L = m·R, where m is the LCM of the denominators of the terms; opening brackets and combining like terms rewrites each side as an equal expression
relations.meaning: An equation is brought to a simpler form, without changing its solution, by opening brackets and combining like terms on both sides and by multiplying both sides by the LCM of the denominators of its terms.

symbols.meaning: The two sides of the equation
The LCM of the denominators of all terms on both sides

conditions: Every term inside a bracket is multiplied by the factor in front of it, sign included.
Both whole sides are multiplied by the LCM, including terms that have no denominator, even when fractions appear on one side only.
Like terms are combined within one side; terms cross the equality sign only by a balanced operation.
Denominators are non-zero constant integers; the domain is declared before clearing them.

relations.expression: If reducing removes the variable: a false statement (e.g. 6 = 5) ⇒ no solution (contradiction); a true statement (e.g. 6 = 6) ⇒ every value is a solution (identity)
relations.meaning: After reversible reduction, a false constant equality has no admissible solutions; a true constant equality admits every value in the declared domain.

symbols.meaning: The variable-free statement left after reduction

conditions: The variable terms on the two sides cancel completely during reduction.
The verdict is read from the variable-free statement that remains, not from a value of x.
Every reduction preserves the original admissible domain and solution set.

relations.expression: ax + by + c = 0, where a, b, c are real numbers and a and b are not both zero; a solution is a pair (x₀, y₀) with ax₀ + by₀ + c = 0
relations.meaning: A linear equation in two variables has infinitely many solutions; its graph is a straight line, and every point on that line represents a solution.

symbols.meaning: The two variables
The coefficients of x and y
The constant term
One solution, written as an ordered pair

conditions: a and b are not both zero; either individual coefficient may be zero.
a, b and c are real numbers.
The graph claim uses the real Cartesian plane and ordered real pairs.

relations.expression: y = ax + b (a straight line with slope a)
relations.meaning: The form y = ax + b describes every nonvertical line in the real Cartesian plane, including horizontal lines with a = 0. A vertical line x = k has no slope in this form.

symbols.meaning: The slope of the line (not the coefficient a of ax + by + c = 0)
The constant term of the line (not the coefficient b of ax + by + c = 0)

conditions: x and y are real coordinates in the Cartesian plane.
The line is nonvertical; the coefficient of y in the general form is non-zero.
The letters a and b here name slope and constant; they differ from the a and b of ax + by + c = 0.

validity_conditions: Use each relation only under its own explicitly declared domain and conditions.

reasoning_sequence.action: Declare the domain, apply reversible operations, and check zero-coefficient branches.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Inverse operations preserve equality; the two line branches follow by division by whichever coefficient is nonzero.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Either zero coefficient prevents a real-plane line.
misconceptions.counterexample: x = 2 has a = 1, b = 0 and is a vertical line; y = 3 is horizontal.
misconceptions.repair: Exclude both zero together, then divide by whichever coefficient is nonzero.

problem_families.title: Distinguish the declared-domain identity from a contradiction
hidden_invariants: Only reversible operations preserve all admissible solutions.

difficulty.note: Conceptually foundational and frequently skipped, which is why later sign and division errors are so hard to diagnose.

falsification_cases.mutation: Change scope_class to PRESCRIBED with no curriculum binding.
